topIssues.title: Consensus-layer sync fails with pruned history unavailable after upgrading to op-reth v2.3.2
topIssues.author: Creamers158
topIssues.body:
After upgrading op-reth from v2.3.1 to v2.3.2 (while keeping the consensus-layer component at v1.19.1), the rollup node fails to initialize when using consensus-layer sync.

The same configuration works correctly with op-reth v2.3.1.

`t=2026-06-26T09:37:09+0000 lvl=error msg="Error initializing the rollup node" err="failed to init L2: failed to get L2 genesis blockhash: failed to determine L2BlockRef of height 0, could not get payload: pruned history unavailable" t=2026-06-26T09:37:09+0000 lvl=crit msg="Application failed" message="failed to setup: unable to create the rollup node: failed to init L2: failed to get L2 genesis blockhash: failed to determine L2BlockRef of height 0, could not get payload: pruned history unavailable"`

**Working (op-reth v2.3.1)**

```
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8545 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"eth_getBlockByNumber","params":["0x0",false],"id":1}'
```

Returns the expected genesis block:
```
{
  "result": {
    "number": "0x0",
    "hash": "0x8ed4903b7f9c3f7bb7a09374d63ae9c9852cd9aab1784b433c41dbeb47b4dba2",
    ...
  }
}
```

**Failing (op-reth v2.3.2)**

**Running the same RPC request returns:**

```
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "error": {
    "code": 4444,
    "message": "pruned history unavailable"
  }
}
```

**Tracing the error in the source shows:**

ProviderError::BlockExpired
    ↓
EthApiError::PrunedHistoryUnavailable
    ↓
RPC error 4444 ("pruned history unavailable")

**Expected behavior**

When switching the execution layer to consensus sync mode, op-node should initialize successfully, as it does with op-reth v2.3.1.

During initialization, op-node resolves the L2 genesis block (height 0). eth_getBlockByNumber("0x0") is expected to return the L2 genesis block rather than 4444: pruned history unavailable, allowing consensus sync to start.

topPRs.title: feat(kona): integrate kona-sp1 into the monorepo
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
Closes #18489 and closes #18457.

## Summary

Adds the experimental **kona-sp1** integration — zkVM-based fault proofs for OP Stack state transitions, built on [SP1](https://github.com/succinctlabs/sp1) — under `rust/kona/sp1/`.

> ⚠️ **Experimental.** Establishes the crate structure and host/guest baseline. Not wired into production proving; not for production use.

## Provenance

Derived from [OP-Succinct](https://github.com/succinctlabs/op-succinct) via the standalone op-rs/kona prototype at https://github.com/op-rs/kona/pull/3051 (SP1 v5.2.2). That PR was cut from an older op-succinct (≈ v3.3.5); this PR re-aligns the host/client crates to current op-succinct, then adapts everything to the monorepo and SP1 v6.2.4.

## Scope

Ports only the **proving core**: op-succinct's `utils/{client,host,build,ethereum}` and the `range`/`aggregation` guest programs. Excludes op-succinct's `validity`, `fault-proof`, `contracts`, `bindings`, `scripts`, `signer`, and `proof` subsystems, and the host modules `block_range`, `l1_selection`, `proof_cache`, `rpc_types`, `witness_cache`. Benchmarking tooling lands separately.

## Changes vs https://github.com/op-rs/kona/pull/3051

Source is structurally inherited (same `kona-sp1-*` crates and layout). On top of it:

- **SP1 v5.2.2 (`inphi/sp1` fork) → v6.2.4 (official crates.io)**; drives the EVM/precompile API updates and ELF changes below.
- **Re-aligned host/client crates to current op-succinct** (the op-rs PR predated these): the GHSA-5jh4-3p33-85xc target-downgrade postcondition, `OpPrecompiles::new_with_spec` precompile construction, SafeDB JSON-RPC error classification, rollup-config caching/validation, KZG `Ok(false)` rejection, the network-prover builder, and panic-elimination.
- **Collapsed the range ELF variants** (`range-elf-bump` + `range-elf-embedded`) into a single `range-elf` (embedded-allocator feature removed in SP1 v6.2.4).
- **Isolated guest crypto patches** into a nested workspace; gitignored generated ELFs.
- Monorepo wiring: workspace members/deps, `deny.toml`, CI protobuf install, `just build-sp1`.

## Changes vs upstream op-succinct

At the **logic level the host/client crates track current op-succinct** (per the re-alignment above). The remaining differences:

**Structure / layout:**
- Crates renamed `op-succinct-*` → `kona-sp1-*`; `utils/` → `crates/`, Kona module layout.
- **Ethereum DA only** — Celestia, EigenDA, and AltDA range programs and their `utils/{celestia,eigenda,altda}` crates are not ported.
- `range/ethereum` + `range/utils` merged into one `range` crate.
- Added Kona-layer crates with no upstream equivalent: `crates/elfs`, `crates/proof`.

**Toolchain:**
- **SP1 v6.2.4** vs op-succinct's **v6.1.0** — pulls in a newer revm/op-revm/alloy-op-evm precompile API (`PrecompileHalt` vs `PrecompileError`, `OpTx`/`OpEvmContext` types, the gas-`reservoir` arg, fluent `Context::mainnet()…build` builder, `report.gas()`).
- A single `range-elf` (no bump/embedded variants).

**Monorepo integration:**
- Guest crypto patches **isolated in a nested `programs/Cargo.toml` workspace** (own `Cargo.lock` + `[patch.crates-io]` for sha2/sha3/crypto-bigint/k256/p256/substrate-bn), so they don't touch the monorepo `rust/` graph (upstream keeps them at its repo root).
- Generated ELFs **gitignored**; `crates/elfs/build.rs` writes empty placeholders when absent, and real ELFs build on demand via `just build-elfs`.
- Host crates wired into the monorepo `rust/` workspace.

**Monorepo-API adaptations** (newer kona/alloy than op-succinct ships):
- `is_interop_active(block_info.timestamp)` (op-succinct passes `number`).
- Blob lookups take `&[B256]` (not `&[IndexedBlobHash]`); extra `None` arg on `OraclePipeline::new`.
- `PostExecEvmFactoryHooks`/`PostExecEvmFactoryAdapter` from the monorepo's `alloy-op-evm`.
- Host-args wiring (`l2_chain_id` populated, `DataFormat::Directory`).

**Port-specific behavior:**
- A **zero-step / trace-extension short-circuit** in the witness executor: when the claimed L2 block equals the agreed safe head there is nothing to derive, so it asserts `claimed_output_root == agreed_output_root` and returns early. Lifted verbatim from kona's native client (`rust/kona/bin/client/src/single.rs`) so the SP1 client handles the same dispute-game edge case; op-succinct only guards `claimed < safe_head`.

**Unchanged:** the guest commitment scheme matches op-succinct (range commits `BootInfoStruct` via `sp1_zkvm::io::commit`; aggregation digests via `bincode::serialize`).

## File mapping (op-succinct → this PR)

| op-succinct | this PR (`rust/kona/sp1/`) |
|---|---|
| `utils/client` (`op-succinct-client-utils`) | `crates/client` (`kona-sp1-client-utils`) |
| `utils/host` (`op-succinct-host-utils`) | `crates/host` (`kona-sp1-host-utils`) |
| `utils/build` (`op-succinct-build-utils`) | `crates/build` (`kona-sp1-build-utils`) |
| `utils/ethereum/client` | `crates/ethereum/client` (`kona-sp1-ethereum-client-utils`) |
| `utils/ethereum/host` | `crates/ethereum/host` (`kona-sp1-ethereum-host-utils`) |
| `programs/range/ethereum` + `programs/range/utils` | `programs/range` (merged) |
| `programs/aggregation` | `programs/aggregation` |
| — (no upstream equivalent) | `crates/elfs`, `crates/proof` |

`crates/client/src/{boot,client,types,oracle/*,precompiles/*,witness/*}` and `crates/host/src/{constants,contract,fetcher,host,logger,metrics,network,proof,stats,witness_generation/*}` map 1:1 to op-succinct's `utils/client/src` and `utils/host/src`.

## Known gaps / follow-ups

- Only the **guest programs** (range, aggregation) are included — no host-side programs; the host crates are libraries only.
- Monorepo CI does not yet install the SP1 toolchain or run the Dockerized ELF build, Codecov wiring, or no-std checks for the SP1 crates (#18326).
- We'll likely want to **rename the crates** once this is made more independent from SP1 and supports different zkVMs.
- Benchmarking harness lands separately.
- It's possible the roundtrip serialization of proof/public values between the range proof and agg proof do not match exactly due to `bincode` weirdness. This can be fixed in a follow-up PR if needed (requires generating two real, full range proofs and aggregating them in one agg proof); this PR chose to minimize changes from upstream op-succinct instead.

topPRs.title: feat(kona-safedb): port op-node SafeDB to Rust
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds the **`kona-safedb`** crate — a 1-to-1 Rust port of the op-node `safedb` package. It records, per L1 block, the L2 safe head that derivation reached as of that block, used by systems (fault proofs, interop) that need a high-quality derivation record. kona-node previously had no equivalent.

The on-disk key/value encoding is byte-exact with the Go implementation, so a database is interchangeable between the two.

## What's included

- **`SafeDbV1` trait** — the versioned database interface, mockable via `#[cfg_attr(test, mockall::automock)]` (generates `MockSafeDbV1`).
- **`SafeDb`** — rocksdb-backed implementation. All Go methods ported: `safe_head_updated`, `safe_head_reset`, `safe_head_at_l1`, `first_entry`, `last_entry`, `l1_at_safe_head`, `enabled`, `close`.
- **`DisabledDb`** — no-op implementation (port of `disabled.go`).
- The rocksdb backend is behind a **non-default `rocksdb` feature**, so consumers needing only the trait/`DisabledDb` avoid the rocksdb/libclang build dependency. Default `cargo build --workspace` does not pull rocksdb; `--all-features` (used by CI test/clippy) builds and exercises everything.
- Iterators are bounded to the key column, mirroring the Go `IterRange`.

## Testing

- Full Go test suite ported (store/reopen persistence, reset truncation edge cases, `l1_at_safe_head` table, decode/ordering).
- Added exact-byte-layout tests (locking cross-impl interop) and a backend-error test.
- `--all-features`: 30 tests pass. Default: build is warning-free. `clippy --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo doc -D warnings`, `cargo +nightly fmt --check`, and `cargo hack check --feature-powerset` all clean.

## Out of scope (follow-up)

Node integration — `SafeHeadListener`-style derivation hook, the `optimism_safeHeadAtL1` RPC handler, and the CLI/config flag to enable it. The `SafeDbV1` trait is the seam those will build on.

topPRs.title: feat(kona-sp1): scaffold super interop programs
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

This PR adds the initial SP1 super interop proof shape for ZK dispute games.

It introduces shared public IO types for the unified super-range program and final super-aggregation program, including super-root encoding and final public-value encoding that match the tuple verified by `ZKDisputeGame.prove`.

The output-root range and consolidation proofs are now handled by a single unified super-range program with (optimistic output-root) range and consolidation modes, so aggregation verifies one semantic class of proof with one `range_vkey`.

The guest execution logic is intentionally still incomplete in this PR. The aggregation program accepts the range vkey dynamically for now, and the range/consolidation verification bodies are left as TODOs for the follow-up implementation work.

## Program Input Validation

This PR also introduces logic to validate the program input shape. This validation is complementary to the more involved super-STF operations, ensuring that the super-aggregation program verifies that all required proofs are well-formed and provided.

### Super-range input validation

The unified super-range program first validates the mode-specific input shape.
For range mode, it checks:

- the timestamp span is valid
- chain IDs are non-empty and strictly increasing
- claimed transitions cover exactly every (timestamp, chain_id) pair in span order
- each transition’s timestamp and chain ID match the expected position

For consolidation mode, it checks:

- the timestamp span is valid
- there is one consolidation input per timestamp
- each claimed super-root proof has the expected timestamp
- each super-root proof uses the supported version and ordered chain set
- optimistic blocks are non-empty, strictly ordered, and match the claimed super-root proof’s chain coverage
- every timestamp uses the same chain set

### Super-aggregation input validation

Aggregation validates the declared range public outputs before recursive proof verification.
It checks:

- `starting_super_root_proof` hashes to `starting_root_hash`
- there is at least one range output and one consolidation output
- the disputed interval starts at `starting_super_root.timestamp + 1`
- consolidation outputs cover the full timestamp interval contiguously
- consolidation `previous_super_root` values chain forward from `starting_root_hash`
- the final consolidated root equals `root_claim`
- range outputs cover the same full timestamp interval contiguously
- every range output commits to the same `l1_head` as the game
- every range output’s `previous_super_root` matches the super root before that range
- range optimistic blocks match the corresponding consolidation optimistic blocks timestamp by timestamp
- all range/consolidation outputs use the chain set from the starting super root

## Meta

part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21459
